figures.caption: Fig. 1 | Stress monitoring and mechano-electrochemical coupling relationships. a In situ monitoring of expansion force variations in a Li|Bare solid polymer electrolyte (SPE)|Li symmetric pouch cell at 0.1 mA/cm2. b 2D stress distribution in the Li|Bare SPE|Li symmetric pouch cell at different cycles. c Stress monitoring in a Li|Bare SPE|Li symmetric pouch cell after 50,000 s Li plating/stripping via 3D stress visualization technique. d The finite element method (FEM) simulation result of the stress response property of bare SPE at different stress propagation periods (Time 1 indicates the initial stage. Time 2 indicates the middle stage). e Visualization of the stress response within a specific horizontal line (white dashed line in d) parallel to the X-axis based on FEM simulation in the bare SPE system. f Stress variation over time at the point where X = 0 on the white dashed line based on FEM simulation in the bare SPE system. g The schematic of the mechano-electrochemical coupling relationships in the bare SPE system. Phase field model (PFM) simulation results of galvanostatic cycling under the modulation of h bare SPE system and i layered SPE system. In simulation with the applied current density of 0.2 mA/cm2 for 3600 s Li plating.

figures.caption: Fig. 2 | Fabrication and characterization of the layered SPE. a Schematic illustration of the layered SPE featuring amorphous tablets and multiscale crosslinked interfaces. b Optical photograph of large-scale synthesis of 2D amorphous SiO2 NSs. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) (c), atomic force microscopy (AFM) (d), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (e) images of SiO2 NSs, showing thin features. f High-resolution TEM image of SiO2 NSs. The insert is the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of amorphous SiO2 NSs. g Digital photograph of a 1-m-long roll of the layered SPE film. h Cross-section SEM image of the layered SPE film, showing a densely interlaced, homogeneously stacked and layered arrangement. i Corresponding Si element energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping.

figures.caption: Fig. 3 | Micromechanical and macromechanical properties of layered SPE. a Representative scheme for one-direction (Z) probing of nanoindentation contact response. Young's modulus (b) and hardness (c) of electrolyte films measured by static nanoindentation test. Typical contour maps of Young's modulus distribution (d) and hardness distribution (e) for layered SPE obtained from a scanning area of 60 μm × 60 μm. Typical contour maps of Young's modulus distribution (f) and hardness distribution (g) for bare SPE obtained from a scanning area of 60 μm × 60 μm. 3D AFM Young's modulus mappings of layered SPE (h) and bare SPE (i). All the mechanical tests are conducted at 25 ± 2 °C with 25% relative humidity (RH).

figures.caption: Fig. 4 | Electrochemical and physicochemical properties of layered SPE. a Arrhenius plots of the electrolytes. "Layered SPE-xSiO2" refers to the PEO-LiTFSI-xSiO2 system (Li+: EO = 1:16), and x refers to the mass ratio of SiO2 NSs to PEO. b Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) profiles of electrolytes from 0 to 100 °C. c The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves of Li|Layered SPE-0.3 SiO2|SS and Li|Bare SPE|SS cells at a scan rate of 1 mV/s at 60 °C. d Li+ transference number test and polarization curve of layered SPE-0.3 SiO2 with the inserted electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) before and after the polarization tested at 60 °C. e 7Li solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra of SPEs and LiTFSI for comparison. f Raman spectra of electrolytes. g Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) analysis of PEO, bare SPE, and layered SPE-0.3 SiO2, with enlarged views of the 1300–1400 and 1020–1180 cm−1 regions. h Density functional theory (DFT) simulations of the structures of the PEO chain and amorphous SiO2.

figures.caption: Fig. 5 | Modulation of layered SPE in Li plating/stripping stability, morphology, and component evolution of Li metal electrode. Li plating/stripping stability of symmetric coin cells at 0.1 mA/cm2, cutoff capacity of 0.05 mA h/cm2 under 60 °C (a) and 30 °C (b). Ex situ SEM (c) and 3D AFM images (d) of the Li metal electrode after 300 h Li plating/stripping at 60 °C with 0.1 mA/cm2, obtained from the Li|Bare SPE|Li symmetric cell under Ar atmosphere. Ex situ SEM (e) and 3D AFM images (f) of the Li metal negative electrode after 300 h Li plating/stripping at 60 °C with 0.1 mA/cm2 obtained from the Li|Layered SPE|Li symmetric cell. g Li 1s and O 1s X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectra were conducted on the Li metal electrode surface after 300 h Li plating/stripping. h In situ monitoring of internal expansion force variations in a 50 mm × 50 mm Li|Layered SPE|Li symmetric pouch cell at 30 °C with 0.1 mA/cm2. i Stress maps for a Li|Layered SPE|Li pouch cell at different cycles at 30 °C with 0.1 mA/cm2. j Visualization of stress growth in a Li|Layered SPE|Li pouch cell plating/stripping at 30 °C with 0.1 mA/cm2 via a 3D real-time visualization technique.
